steps.title: Import React and hooks from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all these named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and hooks
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and hooks from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'react' package is imported with the specified hooks, making them available for use in your custom hook.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the necessary hooks. This gives you the building blocks for creating your custom session timeout hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement is incomplete or contains errors. Make sure you're importing React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import React, useState, useEffect, useRef, and useCallback from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the useSessionTimeout hook function
steps.instruction: Create a function called useSessionTimeout that takes timeoutInMinutes as a parameter and returns an object with isActive and resetSession properties.
steps.hint: Define a function named useSessionTimeout with a parameter for timeoutInMinutes. The function should return an object containing isActive and resetSession properties.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

// Create the useSessionTimeout hook function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named useSessionTimeout is defined with the correct parameter and return type structure.
successCriteria: The code should contain a function named useSessionTimeout that accepts timeoutInMinutes as a parameter and returns an object with isActive and resetSession properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the useSessionTimeout hook function with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named exactly 'useSessionTimeout', accepts a timeoutInMinutes parameter, and returns an object with both isActive and resetSession properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function called useSessionTimeout that takes timeoutInMinutes as a parameter and returns an object with isActive and resetSession properties.

steps.title: Add TypeScript interface for the hook's return type
steps.instruction: Inside the useSessionTimeout hook file, create a TypeScript interface called SessionTimeoutReturn that defines the hook's return type. It should have two properties: isActive (boolean) and resetSession (a function that returns void).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions. Remember to use TypeScript syntax for function types.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a TypeScript interface that clearly defines the shape of data your custom hook will return.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the TypeScript interface for your hook's return type. This provides clear type safety for the values your hook will return.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your interface includes both required properties with the correct TypeScript types. Make sure you have 'isActive: boolean' and 'resetSession: () => void'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a TypeScript interface named SessionTimeoutReturn with two properties: isActive (boolean) and resetSession (a function that returns void).

steps.title: Initialize isActive state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the useSessionTimeout hook function, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'isActive' initialized to true. Make sure to include the proper TypeScript type annotation for boolean.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The syntax is: const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState<boolean>(true);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(true);
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook will have an isActive state variable initialized to true with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: Initial value is set to true
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isActive state variable with proper TypeScript typing. This will track whether the user's session is currently active.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all required elements: the useState hook call, naming the variable 'isActive', adding the <boolean> type annotation, and setting the initial value to true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isActive state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState<boolean>(true) inside the hook function to create the state variable.

steps.title: Create timeoutRef with useRef
steps.instruction: Inside your useSessionTimeout hook, create a timeoutRef using useRef to store the timeout ID. Use the type NodeJS.Timeout | null and initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Use the useRef hook from React with the appropriate TypeScript type annotation.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a ref for a timeout ID
const timeoutRef = useRef<NodeJS.Timeout | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A timeoutRef variable is created using useRef with the correct TypeScript type, ready to store timeout IDs.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ref to store the timeout ID. This will persist across renders without causing re-renders.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useRef with the correct TypeScript type (NodeJS.Timeout | null) and initializing it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a ref using useRef to store the timeout ID. Remember to specify the TypeScript type and initialize it.

steps.title: Define resetSession function with useCallback
steps.instruction: Inside your useSessionTimeout hook, define a function named resetSession using useCallback. This function should set isActive to true and clear any existing timeout stored in timeoutRef.current.
steps.hint: Use useCallback to memoize the function. Inside it, call setIsActive(true) and clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current).
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a memoized resetSession function that resets the session state and clears any pending timeout.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a memoized resetSession function that will reset the session state and clear any existing timeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your resetSession function includes all required elements: uses useCallback, sets isActive to true, and clears the timeout reference.
steps.feedbackWrong: This doesn't match what we need. Remember to create a function named resetSession using useCallback that sets isActive to true and clears timeoutRef.current.

steps.title: Create startTimeout function
steps.instruction: Inside your useSessionTimeout hook, define a function named startTimeout that will set a timeout to change isActive to false after the specified timeoutInMinutes. This function should use the existing timeoutRef and setActive state setter.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setTimeout to schedule setting isActive to false after converting minutes to milliseconds. Store the timeout ID in timeoutRef.current.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a startTimeout function that uses setTimeout to schedule setting isActive to false after the specified timeout period.
successCriteria: The startTimeout function should be defined inside the hook, use setTimeout, store the timeout ID in timeoutRef.current, and call setActive(false) in the timeout callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the startTimeout function that will handle the session timeout countdown.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the startTimeout function, but it's missing some key elements. Make sure it uses setTimeout, stores the timeout ID in timeoutRef.current, and calls setActive(false) after the timeout period.
steps.feedbackWrong: The startTimeout function isn't defined correctly. It should be a function that uses setTimeout to schedule setting isActive to false after the timeoutInMinutes period.

steps.title: Set up event listeners in useEffect
steps.instruction: Add a useEffect hook inside your useSessionTimeout function to set up event listeners for user activity. The useEffect should add event listeners for 'mousemove', 'keydown', and 'click' events that call the resetSession function when triggered.
steps.hint: Use useEffect with an empty dependency array to run setup code once. Inside, add event listeners to the document for the three events, each calling resetSession. Return a cleanup function that removes the event listeners.
steps.expectedOutcome: A useEffect hook is added that sets up event listeners for user activity and properly cleans them up.
successCriteria:
The useEffect should:
1. Add event listeners for 'mousemove', 'keydown', and 'click' events
2. Call resetSession when any of these events occur
3. Return a cleanup function that removes all three event listeners
4. Have an empty dependency array []
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the useEffect hook with event listeners that will detect user activity and reset the session timeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included all three event listeners ('mousemove', 'keydown', 'click') and that your cleanup function removes all of them.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useEffect setup is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add event listeners for all three activity types and properly clean them up.

steps.title: Clean up timeout and event listeners
steps.instruction: Add a cleanup function inside the existing useEffect that clears the timeoutRef and removes the event listeners for 'mousemove', 'keydown', and 'click'.
steps.hint: Return a function from useEffect that runs when the component unmounts or dependencies change. Inside it, clear the timeout and call removeEventListener for each event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect will now have a proper cleanup function that prevents memory leaks by clearing the timeout and removing event listeners.
successCriteria: The useEffect includes a return statement with a cleanup function
The cleanup function clears timeoutRef.current if it exists
The cleanup function calls removeEventListener for 'mousemove', 'keydown', and 'click' events
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented proper cleanup to prevent memory leaks. The timeout will be cleared and event listeners removed when the component unmounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your cleanup function handles both the timeout and all three event listeners ('mousemove', 'keydown', 'click').
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function should be returned from useEffect and clear the timeoutRef while removing all event listeners. Check the example for the correct structure.

steps.title: Return the hook's values
steps.instruction: Complete the hook by returning an object with the isActive state and resetSession function.
steps.hint: At the end of your hook function, return an object containing the isActive variable and resetSession function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The hook now returns an object with isActive and resetSession, making these values available to any component that uses the hook.
successCriteria: The hook function should end with a return statement that returns an object containing the isActive variable and resetSession function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully returned the hook's state and function, making them available for component consumption.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with both isActive and resetSession properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The hook needs to return an object containing both the isActive state and resetSession function.

steps.title: Create a demo component to test the hook
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named SessionTimeoutDemo that uses the useSessionTimeout hook with a 1-minute timeout.
steps.hint: Define a component that calls useSessionTimeout(1) and returns JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: A SessionTimeoutDemo component is created that uses the useSessionTimeout hook.
successCriteria: The component must be named SessionTimeoutDemo, call useSessionTimeout(1), and return JSX (e.g., a div).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the demo component that will test the session timeout hook.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named SessionTimeoutDemo, calls useSessionTimeout(1), and returns some JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined SessionTimeoutDemo, called useSessionTimeout(1), and returned JSX.

steps.title: Render session status and reset button
steps.instruction: In the SessionTimeoutDemo component, render a paragraph showing the session status and a button that calls resetSession when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the isActive value to conditionally display 'Session active' or 'Session expired'. The button should call resetSession on click.
steps.expectedOutcome: The demo component will display the current session status and provide a button to reset the session timer.
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays session status using isActive
A button element with onClick handler calling resetSession
Conditional text shows 'Active' when isActive is true, 'Expired' when false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the session status and reset button. The component now displays whether the session is active or expired and provides user interaction to reset the timer.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the status paragraph and reset button. The paragraph should conditionally display 'Active' or 'Expired' based on isActive, and the button should call resetSession when clicked.
steps.feedbackWrong: The demo component doesn't properly render the session status and reset button. You need to add JSX that displays the current isActive status and a button that calls resetSession when clicked.
